tips.title: Airbrushing Vallejo Model Air — Thinning Ratio and Pressure
tips.text: Vallejo Model Air is designed for airbrushing, but thinning improves atomization. Mix at a 2:1 ratio with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for optimal flow. Add 3-4 drops of Vallejo Flow Improver per 10 drops of thinned paint for better coverage. Spray at 1.5-2.0 bar pressure. Test on a white plastic spoon — if the paint spiders outward evenly, you're ready to paint.

tips.title: Base Coat Technique with Alclad II — Pre-shading and Sealing
tips.text: Apply Alclad II Chrome or Metal base coats using multiple thin layers. Pre-shade panels with a lighter shade of Alclad II to create depth. Let each coat dry for 30 minutes before applying the next. Seal with Alclad II Micro-Sol or Micro-Surfacer before applying weathering effects.

tips.title: Camouflage Masking — Tamiya Tape and Mr. Hobby Tape
tips.text: For complex camouflage patterns, use Tamiya Masking Tape for straight edges and Mr. Hobby Masking Tape for curved surfaces. Apply tape in a warm, dust-free environment to prevent paint from getting under the edges. Seal with Mr. Hobby Masking Fluid before painting to prevent paint from bleeding.

tips.title: Applying AK Interactive Washes — Dilution and Application
tips.text: AK Interactive Washes are ready to use but can be diluted with AK Interactive Thinner for lighter effects. Dilute at a 1:1 ratio for a stronger wash or 1:2 for a lighter touch. Apply washes with a brush, focusing on panel lines and recesses. Work quickly but carefully, removing excess wash with a damp cloth or cotton swab before it dries.

tips.title: Chipping with Sponge Technique — Scale75 Chipping Medium
tips.text: Apply Scale75 Chipping Medium where you want chips to appear. Allow it to dry completely. Using a damp sponge (not too wet), gently dab the surface to create chips. The wetter the sponge, the larger the chips. Seal with a light coat of Vallejo Acrylic Gloss Varnish before weathering further.
